finding.claim: Any logged-in session can overwrite any lobby by ID (password, observer password, mod DLL file/checksum, map, description). No host/ownership check. High severity, high confidence.
finding.source: Authenticated POST /game/advertisement/update: attacker-chosen id plus password, passworded, modDllFile, modDllChecksum, mapName, description. Precondition: any valid sessionID.
finding.sink: adv.UnsafeUpdate(&q) writes password.value/enabled, modDll.file/checksum, observers.password, mapName, description from client input (server/internal/models/advertisement.go:356-370).

trace.note: Route registered under gameGroup, so SessionMiddleware applies; /update is not in sessAnonymousPaths.
Only checks that sessionID resolves to some session. Nothing binds that session's user to the target advertisement.
i.Bind populates the whole AdvertisementUpdateRequest from client input, including Id.
WithWriteLock(q.Id) locks on the attacker-chosen ID.
GetAdvertisement(q.Id) fetches the victim lobby. update.go never reads the session, so there is no HostId comparison. Compare updateTags.go:62, which does check UnsafeGetHostId() != sess.GetUserId().
adv.UnsafeUpdate(&q) applies client fields to the victim lobby.
adv.password.enabled = advFrom.Passworded; line 370 sets adv.password.value = advFrom.Password.

finding.guards_checked: Session presence (sessionMiddleware.go:23-34). Bind errors (update.go:25). Advertisement existence (update.go:36). No host, owner, or peer membership check. Downstream join.go:70-78 compares joiner values against the lobby values that were just overwritten, so an attacker-set password or mod DLL is what joiners must match.

finding.claim: Any logged-in session can change the state of any lobby by ID. Setting state=1 starts the match for the victim lobby, hides and closes it, and broadcasts MatchStartMessage to all its peers. Medium-high severity, high confidence.
finding.source: Authenticated POST /game/advertisement/updateState: attacker-chosen advertisementid and state. Precondition: any valid sessionID.
finding.sink: adv.UnsafeUpdateState(q.State) (models/advertisement.go:419-428) sets state, visible=false, joinable=false, and startTime. Then wss.SendOrStoreMessage(MatchStartMessage) to every peer (updateState.go:72-85).

trace.note: Route registered under gameGroup with session middleware.
Client-supplied AdvertisementId and State are bound.
GetAdvertisement(q.AdvertisementId) with no session or host lookup, under WithWriteLock.
adv.UnsafeUpdateState(q.State) applies the attacker's state.
Iterates all peers and sends them MatchStartMessage.

finding.guards_checked: Session presence only. No host check, no peer membership check. Compare party/peerAdd.go:28 and party/peerUpdate.go:30, which do enforce host-only actions.

finding.claim: Authentication bypass in cached mode. The local user is chosen from the client-supplied platformUserID before authentication, and the offline fallback checks the victim's 30-day cache deadline. An attacker who knows a victim's platform user ID and can make the upstream auth fail gets a session as the victim. Medium severity, conditional on Authentication=cached (or adaptive with connectivity).
finding.source: Unauthenticated POST /game/login/platformlogin body fields platformUserID and macAddress/alias. Precondition: victim authenticated successfully within 30 days so the cache deadline is set; attacker's upstream auth returns non-200 or fails at transport (e.g. upstream unreachable).
finding.sink: Platformlogin creates a session for u.GetId() (routes/game/login/platformlogin.go:33-39) and returns the sessionId.

trace.note: With Authentication=cached, loginHandler is AuthMiddleware(..., cached=true), wrapped by LoginUserMiddleware at game.go:101.
i.Bind reads platformUserID from the body, unauthenticated.
GetOrCreateUser(... req.PlatformUserId ...) returns the victim's User object (models/user.go:199-248).
Victim user stored in request context before AuthMiddleware runs.
Upstream auth returns non-200 or a transport error, and doRequest calls errorHandler().
errorHandler: cached=true, so it calls AuthMiddlewareOffline(next).
AuthMiddlewareOffline reads u := context user (the victim) and its GetAuth() deadline; valid if deadline is non-zero and after now.
Victim deadline was set to now+30d (authCacheValidity, line 27) when victim last authenticated.
Platformlogin deletes the victim's existing session and creates a new one (line 39) for the victim.

finding.guards_checked: Login route is in sessAnonymousPaths (sessionMiddleware.go:12), so no session check. Upstream auth result is the only control, and the fallback bypasses it. The fallback does not check that the upstream credentials belong to platformUserID. The shipped config.toml sets Authentication='disabled', where no auth exists at all (by design).

finding.claim: Account impersonation in required and cached modes. Upstream auth success is never bound to the body platformUserID. A user with valid credentials for account A can log in as local user B (victim) and overwrite B's in-memory item inventory with A's. Medium-high severity, medium confidence: impact depends on whether the upstream rejects a mismatched platformUserID, which this code does not check.
finding.source: Authenticated-upstream attacker supplies own valid creds in the body and sets platformUserID to victim B's ID (platformlogin.go:17). Precondition: Authentication is required, cached, or adaptive with connectivity.
finding.sink: Victim-scoped side effects: victim deadline set (authMiddleware.go:191-196); victim item map cleared and refilled with attacker's inventory (authMiddleware.go:225-233); session created for victim (platformlogin.go:33-39).

trace.note: User chosen from body platformUserID, not from upstream identity.
Body with attacker creds forwarded to upstream auth.
doRequest succeeds for attacker's valid creds, returns attacker's upstream session.
upstreamSessionId taken from attacker's upstream response. Never compared to req.PlatformUserId.
u is victim's User from context.
Inventory fetched for attacker's upstream profile (authResp[5]), not for B.
u.GetItems().WithReadWrite: clear(*items) then refilled with attacker's items. Victim data is overwritten.
Session issued for victim B.

finding.guards_checked: Upstream success check (authMiddleware.go:128-133). No binding of upstream account or profile to platformUserID. Under Authentication=disabled (shipped default) identity is client-chosen anyway by design, so this only matters for required/cached/adaptive.

finding.claim: Any peer of an advertisement can uninvite any other user from it. No host check. Low severity, medium confidence: the intended authority model is not documented in this code.
finding.source: Authenticated POST /game/invitation/cancelInvitation: attacker-chosen advertisementid and inviteeid. Precondition: caller is a peer in the lobby (peers.Load at line 33).
finding.sink: peer.Uninvite(invitee) (line 44), then CancelInvitationMessage to the invitee (lines 48-58).

trace.note: Lobby looked up by client-supplied AdvertisementId.
Caller must be a peer. Membership is the only check.
Invitee is any client-supplied UserId.
peer.Uninvite(invitee) applied.

finding.guards_checked: Lobby existence, peer membership of caller, invitee existence. No host or role check.

finding.claim: Any logged-in session can mint a new signed credential for an arbitrary key string on every request, before checking that the key exists. Each credential is held in memory for 5 minutes. Low severity: memory growth and DoS, no data exposure.
finding.source: Authenticated GET /game/cloud/getTempCredentials: attacker-chosen key query parameter, unbounded per session.
finding.sink: models.CreateCredential stores a new session in the Credentials map (models/credentials.go:33-35, baseSession.go:42-61).

trace.note: fullKey taken from query.
CreateCredential runs unconditionally, before the loop at line 23 checks whether the key exists.
Each call stores a new entry with a fresh id from generateSignature.

finding.guards_checked: Session required (not anonymous). No rate limit or cap on store size. Get (baseSession.go:63) does not check expiry, so entries live until the sweeper removes them.
